title: Bagel and Lox Breakfast Board
subtitle: Toasted bagels with lox, cream cheese, capers, and fixings for ten.
description: Adapted from classic New York deli appetizing tradition for firehall self-serve breakfast: assorted bagels toasted crisp with platters of lox, cream cheese, capers, red onion, tomato, and cucumber for ten firefighters.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Bagel and Lox Breakfast Board in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch Eggs. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Prep all fixings
steps.instruction: Slice onion, tomato, and cucumber and arrange in separate bowls on ice or cold trays. Drain capers and portion cream cheese into ramekins. Keep lox refrigerated until the board goes out. Plan about 15 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew.

steps.title: Toast the bagels
steps.instruction: Split bagels and toast on sheet pans at 350°F until edges are crisp, about 6 minutes. Hold in a warm oven uncovered at 200°F—do not stack or they steam soft. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Arrange the board
steps.instruction: Center lox on a large chilled platter folded in overlapping layers. Surround with ramekins of cream cheese, capers, onion, tomato, cucumber, and lemon wedges. Plan about 8 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Set up the serving line
steps.instruction: Place toasted bagels in a warm basket at the line with tongs. Post a simple build order: schmear, lox, capers, onion, tomato. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Serve and refresh
steps.instruction: Serve immediately as a self-serve board. Refresh lox and cold fixings on ice if service runs longer than 30 minutes to keep fish food-safe. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

stationWorkflow: Keep lox on ice until the moment the board hits the table—room temp fish is a food-safety issue.
Toast bagels in two sheet pan batches so all ten finish crisp at the same time.
Assign one crew member to restock fixings while another manages bagel refills.
cleanupNotes: Discard any lox held above 40°F for more than 2 hours—do not save for later shifts.
Wash onion and caper boards separately from bagel crumbs to avoid cross-smells.
leftovers: Unused cream cheese and capers keep; repurpose lox in scrambled eggs within 24 hours if chilled.
Day-old bagels make excellent French toast sticks with cinnamon sugar.
